title: Efficient Adaptable Streaming Aggregation Engine
problem: Aggregation queries on grouped and time-series data suffer from high hardware utilization and random memory access patterns when implemented with hash-based approaches or multi-tasking mechanisms.
motivation: Aggregation queries are computationally demanding analytics operations requiring efficient hardware acceleration for large-scale data processing.
method: Instead of using hash tables that cause random, inefficient memory access, this method uses a reconfigurable pipeline—a series of processing stages that automatically adjust themselves based on the aggregation task you're performing (like grouping data or computing time-series values). The pipeline arranges data flow to keep memory access sequential and predictable, so complex queries process quickly without wasting hardware resources.
key_novelty: This approach replaces hash-based aggregation with a reconfigurable pipeline that adapts to different task types, eliminating inefficient random memory access patterns.
contributions: Reconfigurable pipeline architecture supporting diverse aggregation queries
Reduced hardware utilization compared to hash-based approaches
High-throughput streaming design for grouped and time-series data
Support for dynamic task adaptation with minimal reconfiguration overhead
